subject: Future Tech
title: Stimulating Neurons
description: A quick, practical guide to Stimulating Neurons.

hook.text: BCIs don't just read the brain. Some send signals back in, stimulating neurons to create sensations or alter mood.

buildup.text: Tiny electrical pulses delivered to specific brain areas can trigger feelings of touch, sound, or even color.

discovery.text: Wilder Penfield mapped this in the 1950s by stimulating patients' brains during surgery. They reported vivid memories.

twist.text: Stimulation is crude compared to reading. We can poke the brain, but targeting precise sensations remains difficult.

climax.text: Closed-loop BCIs aim to read and write simultaneously, creating a two-way conversation between brain and machine.

punchline.text: Reading the brain was step one. Writing is step two.

quiz.question: Who first mapped brain functions by electrically stimulating patients during surgery?
